reason: Free ChatGPT, NotebookLM, and campus Drive exam banks already cost $0, and since AI tools have burned me on quant formulas before, I'd still end up checking every step myself. As a TA and tutor in a normal week, I'd rather stick to the Drive past papers and my own worked notes than pay for another PDF cram tool.
objection: 'Dual-Model Math Verifier' sounds like two AIs checking each other, and a refund guarantee doesn't pay back lost cram hours or embarrassment in front of tutees if a subscript or derivation step is wrong.
would_change_my_mind: Running the free 5-question preview on one of our hardest messy past-exam PDFs and seeing zero formula or subscript errors—ideally backed by transparent calculation checks rather than just LLM guesses—so it actually saves me review-prep time.
